source.author: stat
source.text: ecce et Dircaeae iuxta dux concitus alae venerat Amphion; non longum caede recenti laetatus videt innumeris fervere catervis tellurem atque una gentem exspirare ruina, qui tremor elicita caeli de lampade tactis, hic fixit iuvenem, pariterque horrore sub uno vox, acies sanguisque perit, gemitusque parantem ipse ultro convertit equus; fugit ala retorto pulvere, nondum illi Thebarum claustra subibant, et iam Argiva cohors nocturno freta triumpho prosilit in campos; per et arma et membra iacentum taetraque congerie sola semianimumque cruorem cornipedes ipsique ruunt: gravis exterit artus ungula, sanguineus lavat imber et impedit axes.
source.text_original: ecce et Dircaeae iuxta dux concitus alae / venerat Amphion; non longum caede recenti / laetatus videt innumeris fervere catervis / tellurem atque una gentem exspirare ruina, / qui tremor elicita caeli de lampade tactis, / hic fixit iuvenem, pariterque horrore sub uno / vox, acies sanguisque perit, gemitusque parantem / ipse ultro convertit equus; fugit ala retorto / pulvere, nondum illi Thebarum claustra subibant, / et iam Argiva cohors nocturno freta triumpho / prosilit in campos; per et arma et membra iacentum / taetraque congerie sola semianimumque cruorem / cornipedes ipsique ruunt: gravis exterit artus / ungula, sanguineus lavat imber et impedit axes.
source.text_english: And behold, Amphion too had come, leader of the band from Dirce’s side, roused to action; not long delighted by the recent slaughter, he sees the earth seething with countless swarms and the whole race breathing out its life in one ruin. Such was the terror that from the loosed fire of heaven on the touched men, here it fixed a youth, and together, under a single dread, voice, battle line, and blood perish; and the horse itself, of its own accord, turned back the rider who was preparing a cry. The wing fled with the dust whipped round; still not yet were the barriers of Thebes closing on them, and already the Argive cohort, trusting in its nocturnal triumph, bounds out into the fields. Over weapons and limbs of the fallen, and through the hideous heap and the half-dead gore, the hoofed horses rush, and the riders themselves: the heavy hoof crushes the limbs, a bloody rain washes them and hinders the chariots.

reuse.text: fervere cuncta virum coetu, simul undique cernit delatum nemus et docta resonare bipenni litora; iam pinus gracili dissolvere lamna Thespiaden iungique latus lentoque sequaces molliri videt igne trabes, remisque paratis Pallada velifero quaerentem bracchia malo.
reuse.text_original: fervere cuncta virum coetu, simul undique cernit / delatum nemus et docta resonare bipenni / litora; iam pinus gracili dissolvere lamna / Thespiaden iungique latus lentoque sequaces / molliri videt igne trabes, remisque paratis / Pallada velifero quaerentem bracchia malo.
reuse.text_english: he sees all things seething with a company of men, and at the same time the grove brought in from every side and the shores echoing with the skilled double axe; already the pine is being split into thin planks, the Thespian joined, and the sides fitted together, and the following timbers softened by the slow fire, and Pallas, with the oars prepared, seeking the arms on the sail-bearing mast.
